title: Capsaicin suppresses microglial inflammation through TRPV1-SSR4 interaction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of microglial response during neuroinflammation, a key pathological feature of various neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease. Capsaicin, the primary pungent component in chili peppers, executes its anti-inflammatory properties as a TRPV1 agonist. Although the mechanism of TRPV1 channel activation and signal transduction by capsaicin has been extensively studied, the protein-protein interaction-based mechanisms by which TRPV1 modulates microglial inflammatory responses in the context of neurodegeneration remains unclear. METHODS: We used a lipopolysaccharide-induced acute neuroinflammation model to examine the effects of TRPV1 activation and pharmacological blockade of TRPV1 channel gating on microglial inflammatory responses. Proximity labeling-based proteomics, bioluminescence resonance energy transfer, and NanoLuc Binary Technology were used to identify and characterize TRPV1-interacting proteins. Signal sequence receptor subunit 4 (SSR4) knockdown and forced interaction between TRPV1 and SSR4 were performed to assess the functional contribution of the TRPV1-SSR4 interaction. Structural modeling, BRET-based domain mapping, and colocalization analyses were further used to examine the molecular and subcellular features of SSR4 recruitment by TRPV1. RESULTS: In the neuroinflammatory model, the TRPV1 agonist capsaicin attenuated pro-inflammatory cytokine production, neuronal apoptosis, microgliosis, and microglial soma enlargement in a TRPV1-dependent manner. Notably, pharmacological blockade of TRPV1 channel gating by capsazepine did not abolish the anti-inflammatory action of capsaicin, suggesting an alternative mechanism of action beyond the canonical ligand-gated Ca2⁺ influx. Screening of TRPV1 prey proteins and validation strategy identified SSR4 as a capsaicin-responsive, TRPV1-associated protein. SSR4 knockdown in microglia significantly diminished the suppression of inflammatory responses caused by TRPV1 activation. Conversely, forced interaction between TRPV1 and SSR4 partially mimicked the anti-inflammatory effects of TRPV1 activation. Further structural and cellular analyses suggested that the transmembrane region of TRPV1 supports SSR4 recruitment. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that capsaicin suppresses microglial inflammation mediated by the TRPV1-SSR4 interaction, providing new insights into the chemical biology basis of TRPV1 interoceptive signaling and potential applications of natural TRPV1 agonists for modifying therapy of neuroinflammation-associated neurodegeneration.

title: Residual monomers and volatile leachable substances of conventional and CAD/CAM-fabricated denture base materials - GC-MS analysis and surface characterization.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Methacrylic acid ester-based resins for denture fabrication release residual monomers and leachable substances that may interact with oral tissues. With increasing adoption of CAD/CAM technologies, a systematic comparison of leachable substance profiles and surface characteristics across polymerization methods is needed. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study compared the chemical composition and profiles of leachable substances of four denture materials - autopolymerized, thermal polymerized, milled, and 3D-printed - using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Surface roughness was evaluated by confocal microscopy. RESULTS: GC-MS screening detected 24 distinct compounds in the solid specimens. Among the MMA/PMMA-based materials, methyl methacrylate content was highest in the thermally polymerized resin, followed by the autopolymerized and milled materials, and absent from the 3D-printed resin, consistent with its MMA-free formulation. MMA levels in the extracts did not exceed those of the negative control in any group. Surface roughness was comparable on the polished face (Ra ≈ 0.21-0.25 μm), consistent with SEM findings but material-dependent on the unpolished, tissue-contacting face (Ra 0.37-1.03 μm). CONCLUSIONS: Both fabrication method and material formulation influence the volatile and semi-volatile extractables of denture resins. As the present GC-MS screening may not reliably capture high-molecular-weight dimethacrylates such as Bis-EMA and UDMA, novel CAD/CAM materials require additional, complementary toxicological evaluation. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The leachable substance profiles of CAD/CAM denture resins, particularly the distinct compounds detected in the 3D-printed material, underscore the need for material-specific biocompatibility data to support informed clinical material selection and patient safety.

title: Investigation of surface and subsurface defects of Cu(111) surface by scanning tunneling microscopy.
abstract: Various types of surface defects are observed using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) on a clean Cu(111) surface. Detailed STM images of defects show an asymmetric structure comprised of a bright protrusion inside a hexagonal depression. Protrusions are consistently aligned in the same direction, Cu[001], on the surface. The defects are observed to interact with one another, as each defect is separated by an integer multiple of half the Fermi wavelength, evident from the quasiparticle interference oscillations resulting from the defects. This interaction is also suspected to dictate the orientation of the defects, resulting in their uniform alignment. Ab initio density functional theory methods are used to investigate Cu(111) surface defects and adatoms. Simulated STM images using the Tersoff-Hamann scheme are compared to STM images. Results are also discussed in the context of existing literature on similar structures.

title: Along-tract statistical mapping of white matter abnormalities in children with SeLECTS.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Emerging evidence suggests that self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS) may reflect atypical neurodevelopment. As WM maturation extends from the second trimester through adolescence, this study aimed to identify regions of delayed or aberrant white matter (WM) development in children with SeLECTS using along-tract statistical mapping for precise localization of microstructural alterations. MATERIALS AND METHODS: 38 children with SeLECTS and 31 healthy controls underwent diffusion-weighted MRI scan. Fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusivity (MD), and radial diffusivity (RD) were derived from the diffusion tensor model. Whole-brain tractography was performed using deterministic EuDX tracking and registered to a standardized bundle atlas in MNI space. Thirty WM tracts per subject were extracted. Linear mixed models within the BUAN tractometry framework were used to assess segment wise group differences, while partial correlations were performed to evaluate associations between diffusion metrics and cognitive performance. FDR correction was applied per bundle for all comparisons. RESULTS: After FDR correction, children with SeLECTS showed increased MD in the forceps minor, midbody of the corpus callosum, right corticospinal tract, right extreme capsule, and bilateral uncinate fasciculi. MD values in the affected WM segments showed negative correlations with performance and full-scale IQ, and the segments showing significant correlations overlapped with those showing significant group differences. CONCLUSIONS: SeLECTS is associated with MD-based microstructural alterations in superficial frontal, temporal, and parietal pathways, potentially indicating delayed white matter maturation.

title: Sex-divergent neurovascular and cognitive effects of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
abstract: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion is the leading risk factor for the development of vascular dementia and is associated with white matter damage and cognitive impairment. Here, we assessed sex differences in vascular and neural pathology and cognitive impairment in the asymmetric carotid arterial stenosis (ACAS) mouse model of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion. Thirty days of ACAS significantly reduced cerebral blood flow, increased microvascular permeability as evidenced by extravasation of IgG and fibrinogen into brain parenchyma, and impaired MCA vasodilation. ACAS also induced white matter damage in the hippocampus and corpus callosum, with greater damage in the corpus callosum of females compared to males. Spatial memory impairments on the Barnes maze were significantly greater in ACAS males than in females. Finally, miRNA analyses revealed upregulated angiogenic miRNA in the hippocampus and cortex in ACAS females and upregulated neuroinflammatory miRNA in the hippocampus and cortex in ACAS males. Together, these findings indicate that the ACAS model produces robust neuropathology and sex differences in spatial memory and miRNA profiles.

title: Dysregulated cholesterol trafficking through ABCA1 drives neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Although brain cholesterol dysregulation is implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD), targeting cholesterol synthesis has shown limited efficacy. Here we identify ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) as a critical regulator of cholesterol homeostasis in PD. We show that ABCA1 expression is elevated in the substantia nigra of postmortem PD brains and in a PD mouse model, with regional analyses revealing preferential alterations in nigral and striatal circuits. Mechanistically, astrocytic ABCA1 drives excessive cholesterol efflux in mice, promoting neuronal cholesterol overload. In neurons, ABCA1 localizes to lysosomes, where it facilitates cholesterol import, leading to cholesterol accumulation, autophagy impairment and α-synuclein pathology. Genetic silencing of Abca1 in either astrocytes or dopaminergic neurons attenuates neurodegeneration and behavioral deficits in vivo. Furthermore, we identify magnesium citrate as an ABCA1 inhibitor and show that it reduces dopaminergic neuronal loss in a PD mouse model. Our findings identify an ABCA1-dependent cholesterol pathway underlying PD pathogenesis and support ABCA1 inhibition as a potential disease-modifying strategy.

title: α-Catenin phosphorylation is tension-sensitive and supports epithelial barrier functions via afadin.
abstract: Zonula adherens junctions (zAJs) are spatially proximal to tight junctions (TJs), in a superstructure known as the apical junctional complex (AJC). A key component of the AJC is a circumferential ring of F-actin, but how actomyosin contractility drives AJC structure and epithelial barrier function is incompletely understood. Here, we show that a central mechanosensitive component of zAJ, α-catenin (α-cat), undergoes force-dependent phosphorylation in an unstructured linker region. This modification in turn primes the α-cat middle region for effector binding. We credential afadin, a TJ/AJ scaffold protein, as a mechanochemical binding partner of α-cat, identifying residues in α-cat required for binding. α-Cat phosphorylation and afadin binding support their co-enrichment at zAJ and barrier function. A mouse model that prevents α-cat phosphorylation is particularly detrimental to postnatal brain development, leading to hydrocephalus with junctional features similar to an afadin-binding mutant form of α-cat. These data support a model where α-cat integrates mechanical and chemical signals to progressively promote zAJ enrichment, effector recruitment, and barrier function.

title: Gαi2 promotes microtubule-driven incorporation of neurofilaments to stabilise nascent axons in vivo.
abstract: Axon initiation is a critical step in the establishment of neuronal morphology. However, the mechanisms regulating stable axon initiation during embryonic development remain poorly understood. Here, using fixed-tissue super-resolution and high-resolution live-tissue imaging in the developing chick spinal cord, we reveal that stable axon initiation is characterised by microtubule-directed neurofilament accumulation in the emerging axon, and identify the multifunctional G-protein Gαi2 as a regulator of this process. Before axon initiation, microtubule network orientation shifts towards the site of the future axon where coiled Gαi2-associated neurofilaments accumulate asymmetrically before unfurling into the initiating axon behind microtubules. Crucially, Gαi2 is associated with neurofilaments and microtubules at their points of contact. Gαi2 depletion reduces engagement between these cytoskeletal networks and leads to impaired passage of neurofilaments into initiating axons and disrupted axon outgrowth, supporting a role for Gαi2 in regulating microtubule-driven incorporation of neurofilaments in nascent axons. These findings advance mechanistic understanding of polarity establishment and provide insight into cytoskeletal regulation during axon formation.

title: An integrated human forebrain organoid reveals microglia-mediated CD8+ T cell recruitment and neuroimmune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease pathology.
abstract: Genetic evidence implicates immune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the neuroimmune mechanisms operating in human tissue remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a modular human forebrain organoid platform that systematically integrates human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia and CD8+ T cells to reconstitute multicellular AD pathology. This system enables functional interrogation of both innate and adaptive immune components in a human-relevant context. Using this platform, we demonstrate that microglia mediate amyloid-β clearance and neuronal maturation but also drive inflammatory activation and recruit CD8+ T cells through CCL4/5 signaling via CCR1/5 and CXCR3, establishing a neuroinflammatory feedback loop. Pharmacological targeting of CCR5 or CXCR3 blocks T cell recruitment and modulates autophagy in a microglia-dependent manner. This modular organoid platform provides a versatile tool for dissecting neuron-immune interactions and enables cell-type-specific therapeutic screening in human neuroinflammatory disease models.

title: Saponin extract from Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge regulates gut-brain axis through intestinal Escherichia coli to reduce cerebral oxidative stress to treat vascular dementia in rodents.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Vascular dementia (VD) is a cognitive dysfunction syndrome caused by cerebrovascular diseases. Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge (AS) has antioxidative, gut microbiota-regulating, and cognitive-improving effects. Escherichia coli (E. coli) abundance is associated with cognitive dysfunction. This study explored the mechanism by which AS improves VD by regulating E. coli along the gut-brain axis, providing a basis for VD drug research and development. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: VD models were established by permanent ligation of the common carotid artery. Morris water maze, Doppler cerebral blood flow measurement, blood lipid assays, pathological staining, Western blot, and ELISA were used to evaluate AS's protective effects on the brain. 16S rRNA sequencing analyzed gut microbiota to screen differential strains. Metabolomics screened endogenous differential metabolites. Oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) was established to evaluate 5-aminovaleric acid effects on neuronal mitochondrial function and oxidative stress. KEY RESULTS: AS significantly improved cognitive dysfunction, restored cerebral blood flow, and attenuated abnormal protein accumulation and oxidative stress in VD rat brains. Microbiota analysis revealed that AS inhibited E. coli proliferation and mitigated associated pathological damage. Furthermore, endogenous metabolite 5-aminovaleric acid alleviated OGD-induced neuronal damage and oxidative stress. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: AS can treat cognitive dysfunction and brain injury in rodents, regulate gut microbiota balance, and reduce the contribution of E. coli. Meanwhile, AS-regulated endogenous metabolite 5-aminovaleric acid can also treat OGD-induced nerve cell injury. These findings suggest that AS may be a promising candidate for VD treatment and provide mechanistic insight into gut-brain axis regulation.

title: Early lineage divergence segregates sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus.
abstract: The thalamus integrates sensory, motor and associative functions through distinct nuclei, yet the developmental principles driving their specification remain unclear. Here we generate a spatiotemporal single-cell multiomic and spatial transcriptomic atlas of the embryonic mouse thalamus, combined with barcoding-based lineage tracing. We identify two major glutamatergic lineages, sensory-related and motor-associative, each governed by different gene regulatory programs and temporal dynamics. These lineages arise from spatially and molecularly distinct progenitor domains, revealing an early segregation of functional identities. Within the sensory lineage, we resolve branching sensory trajectories leading to first-order visual and somatosensory neurons, both emerging from a shared higher-order-like state. Using in silico predictions and in vivo perturbation, we identify Sp9 as a key regulator of visual thalamic fate. Together, our findings define the molecular architecture and developmental trajectories that underpin thalamic modality specification, providing a framework to understand how functional circuits emerge in the mammalian brain.

title: Comprehensive insights into the toxicological disruption of cadmium to juvenile Tachypleus tridentatus: From physiological impairments to multi-omics alterations.
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is highly toxic to aquatic organisms. This study investigated the toxic effects and mechanisms of environmentally relevant Cd concentrations on juvenile Tachypleus tridentatus using physiological, biochemical, lipidomic, and transcriptomic analyses. After 28 days, 0.5 and 5 μg/L Cd significantly inhibited growth, reducing body weight and carapace width. This growth retardation was linked to biphasic molting dysregulation, with initial suppression and subsequent premature activation of chitinase and β-NAGase, disrupting the molting rhythm. Dynamic antioxidant responses were observed: SOD increased only in the 0.5 μg/L group at days 7 and 28, while CAT increased at day 7 but decreased at day 28 in both Cd treatments. The glutathione-dependent pathway was impaired, with no significant MDA elevation. Innate immunity showed a time-dependent pattern: ACP decreased at day 7 in the 5 μg/L group but increased at day 28 in both treatments; AKP increased at day 28 in both treatments; LZM increased at day 7 but decreased at day 28 in both treatments. Key immune-related genes (e.g., Dscam, PGRP-SC2, Ctsz) were downregulated. Lipidomics analysis revealed a global downregulation of core lipids, including triglycerides, diacylglycerols, phosphatidylcholines, and phosphatidylethanolamines, indicating disrupted lipid homeostasis and energy reserve utilization. Transcriptomic profiling further demonstrated that Cd exposure triggered the upregulation of defensive signaling pathways while concurrently downregulating genes associated with the cytoskeleton, cathepsins, and caspase-independent apoptosis, collectively impairing cellular homeostasis and immune function. These findings fill a critical knowledge gap in the ecotoxicological risk assessment of this ancient and endangered species under subchronic, low-level heavy metal exposure.

title: CCKBR signalling controls human definitive endoderm specification and pancreatic lineage differentiation.
abstract: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Paracrine signalling by hormone-producing endocrine cells potentially influences pancreatic development, but this feedback regulation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the roles of gastrin (GAST), cholecystokinin (CCK) and their receptor cholecystokinin B receptor (CCKBR) during human pancreatic development. METHODS: Human iPSCs were differentiated stepwise into definitive endoderm and then the pancreatic endocrine lineage. To assess CCKBR function, CRISPR/Cas9 was used to generate CCKBR-knockout iPSC lines. We profiled transcriptional states by bulk and single-cell RNA-seq with computational analyses, and complemented these with biochemical assays, flow cytometry (FACS) and confocal microscopy. RESULTS: CCKBR expression peaked during definitive endoderm formation and progressively declined during differentiation, remaining detectable in pancreatic progenitors but largely absent from the endocrine lineage. By contrast, GAST and CCK were expressed only transiently during pancreatic progenitor and endocrine lineage formation. Pharmacological activation/inhibition and genetic knockout implicated CCKBR signalling during definitive endoderm formation. Consistently, bulk RNA-seq indicated that CCKBR deletion triggered ectodermal- and mesodermal-associated transcriptional programs and diminished pancreatic lineage specification. During pancreatic induction and lineage formation, sustained CCKBR activation with GAST or CCK attenuated endocrinogenesis and promoted epithelial structure formation. Further analysis revealed the emergence of a pancreatic ductal-like cell formation under prolonged CCKBR stimulation. CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: This study provides mechanistic evidence that the GAST/CCK-CCKBR axis is functionally important during human endoderm and pancreas development. This pathway is repeatedly required during in vitro pluripotent stem cell differentiation, regulating germ-layer formation as well as ductal vs endocrine fate decisions. These findings support the optimisation of pancreatic differentiation protocols and inform future studies on whether this axis contributes to human pancreas development and disease.

title: Schaftoside, a functional flavonoid from fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum L.), alleviates depression and cognitive deficits via the microbiome-gut-brain axis in stressed mice.
abstract: Depression involves dysregulation of central and peripheral networks, with gut microbiota alterations increasingly implicated in pathogenesis. Trigonella foenum-graecum L. (fenugreek), a functional food and medicinal herb, has been used traditionally for neurological disorders, yet its specific neuroprotective constituents remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated the antidepressant potential of schaftoside, the predominant flavonoid of fenugreek seed flavonoids, and explored its mechanisms involving the microbiome-gut-brain axis in a chronic restraint stress (CRS) mouse model. Male Kunming mice were subjected to CRS and orally administered schaftoside (20, 50, and 125 mg kg-1) or fluoxetine (10 mg kg-1) for 28 days. Behavioral assessments (tail suspension, forced swim, novel object recognition, and Y-maze) demonstrated that schaftoside dose-dependently ameliorated depressive-like behaviors and cognitive impairments. It attenuated hippocampal neuronal damage and neuroinflammation, restoring hippocampal 5-HT, NE, and ACh levels. Intestinal barrier integrity was improved, evidenced by enhanced tight junction proteins (ZO-1, occludin) and mucin (MUC2) expression, alongside reduced colonic pro-inflammatory cytokines and elevated IL-10. 16S rRNA profiling revealed that schaftoside reshaped gut microbiota composition, notably suppressing stress-enriched Bacteroides and promoting butyrate-producing Butyricicoccus. Untargeted metabolomics identified restoration of tryptophan and α-linolenic acid metabolism pathways. Spearman correlation analysis revealed significant associations between specific gut genera, fecal metabolites, and host inflammatory/neurochemical markers. Hippocampal transcriptomics indicated enrichment of cAMP signaling, dopaminergic, and serotonergic synapse pathways. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from schaftoside-treated donors partially recapitulated the behavioral, anti-inflammatory, and intestinal barrier-protective effects in antibiotic-pretreated recipient mice, accompanied by restoration of the gut microbiota and metabolite profiles. These findings demonstrate that schaftoside, the major flavonoid of fenugreek seeds, exhibits promising antidepressant-like potential through modulation of the microbiome-gut-brain axis, supporting the functional food application of fenugreek-derived flavonoids for stress-related mood disorders.

title: Temporal regulation of metabolic processes in the marine diazotroph Crocosphaera watsonii WH8501.
abstract: Marine diazotrophic cyanobacteria play a crucial role in oceanic nitrogen cycling, supporting primary production and ecosystem balance. Crocosphaera watsonii WH8501 exemplifies this capability by temporally separating photosynthesis and diazotrophy. To investigate the regulatory mechanisms underlying this process, we employed mass spectrometry-based proteomics in a high-resolution diel culturing experiment, revealing tightly coordinated protein abundance patterns. Unsupervised clustering of diel protein abundance profiles identified six groups of co-regulated proteins characterized by distinct temporal expression patterns and functional categories. Cluster 1 contained nitrogen fixation and amino acid biosynthesis proteins that peaked at night, while cluster 2 included glycogen metabolism and photosynthetic dark reaction proteins that were most abundant during the night and day-night transition, supporting carbon consumption and energy production. Clusters 3 and 4 were enriched in proteins involved in photosynthesis, cell division, and lipid synthesis, with maximal abundance around midday. Cluster 5 comprised peptide biosynthesis proteins that peaked later in the day and may facilitate nitrogenase complex formation. Cluster 6, expressed during the day-night transition, revealed coordinated nitrogenase assembly, with Fe-S cluster proteins preceding peak nitrogenase iron protein abundance, suggesting a temporally ordered sequence of enzyme maturation. Distinct temporal patterns in iron trafficking to heme and Fe-S cluster biosynthetic systems further indicated tightly regulated allocation of iron to metalloproteins across the diel cycle. Together, these results reveal the intricate temporal coordination that enables Crocosphaera to balance nitrogen fixation and photosynthesis within a single cell and underscore the central role of diel regulation in sustaining these globally important processes.IMPORTANCEMarine diazotrophic cyanobacteria play an essential role in global nitrogen cycling and ocean productivity. In this study, we investigate the temporal regulation of Crocosphaera watsonii metabolism using high-resolution proteomics under diel culturing conditions. Our analysis resolves six distinct clusters of protein abundance patterns across the light/dark cycle, reflecting intricate coordination of nitrogen fixation, photosynthesis, carbon allocation, and iron homeostasis. Notably, we identify temporally ordered assembly of nitrogenase subunits, including precursory expression of Fe-S cluster proteins and indications of tightly controlled iron trafficking systems. These findings provide new mechanistic insight into how unicellular diazotrophs synchronize key metabolic processes under natural diel cycles.

title: Integration of polygenic risk with single cell methylation data using met-scDRS.
abstract: MOTIVATION: Although large scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified many risk variants for psychiatric traits their functional implication remain largely unknown. One potential mechanism for their risk is through cellular context-dependent epigenetics such as methylation. Previous methodologies have focused on integrating GWAS with single cell transcriptomics, which allowed identification of within-cell-type heterogeneity in disease risk association. We extended this framework to provide a method called met-scDRS that integrates GWAS with single cell epigenomics and investigates how psychiatric disease risk can manifest through methylomics at single cell resolution. RESULTS: We propose an approach that integrates single cell methylomes with disease associated genes identified from GWAS at single-cell resolution. We found our method to be well calibrated and powered in different scenarios. We then analyzed a publicly available single cell methylome dataset of the human brain for 75 different traits and generated disease relevance scores for each cell for each trait. We find high brain specificity with major cell type enrichments congruent with known findings. We identify within-cell-type heterogeneity for psychiatric disease risk along the brain spatial axis as well as subpopulations that are differentially associated with diseases. Finally, we showed that genes with high correlation between methylation levels and disease relevance scores to be highly enriched in specific functional pathways such as synaptic formation and transmission. AVAILABILITY: met-scDRS is freely available in GitHub as a python package under MIT license: https://github.com/bogdanlab/met-scDRS. Source code is also available from Zenodo with DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21841506. All dataset used in this work are publicly available. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
authors: Li X, Shi Z, Hou K, Eyring KW, Liu C, Heffel MG, Luo C, Geschwind DH, Pasaniuc B

title: Optimization of Atomic Force Microscopy Cantilever Specifications for Pressure Measurement in Biological Tissues.
abstract: PURPOSE: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) is an established technique to measure the mechanical properties of cells and tissues. Measurements are based on force interactions between cantilever and sample. These measurements can be influenced by the underlying substrate. Published literature has utilized this phenomenon to measure the turgor pressure of eukaryotic cells through the cell membrane. The purpose of the current study was to determine how to increase measurement sensitivity of pressure in larger-scale biological tissues, specifically intraocular pressure. METHODS: AFM was used to measure pressurized artificial corneas. Tipless and tipped cantilevers were used to acquire measurements of Young's modulus of elasticity and apparent stiffness over the pressure range: 15, 25, and 35 mmHg to represent normal, elevated, and uncontrolled IOP. RESULTS: In this study, fourteen tipless cantilevers and eight modified cantilevers were tested to determine which cantilever parameters best measured the pressure beneath the tissue. The parameters evaluated were spring constant, indenter tip radius, and effective working length. Spring constant had a more pronounced effect on apparent stiffness than any other parameter examined for both unmodified and modified cantilevers. For modified cantilevers, the ratio of working length to indenter radius enhances the bottom-substrate effect, with lower ratios being more advantageous. CONCLUSION: The results of this study suggest that AFM could be used to quantify pressure beneath biological tissues, but care must be taken to select a cantilever with appropriate specifications.

overview: PURPOSE: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) is an established technique to measure the mechanical properties of cells and tissues.
main: RESULTS: In this study, fourteen tipless cantilevers and eight modified cantilevers were tested to determine which cantilever parameters best measured the pressure beneath the tissue.

title: Stacking-specific two-dimensional In2Se3 for ferroelectric homojunctions.
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectric semiconductors offer unique opportunities for ultrathin non-volatile memory and neuromorphic devices, yet the role of stacking order in intrinsic ferroelectric systems remains largely unexplored. Here we report the stacking-controlled growth of large-area 2D β'- and α-In2Se3 with distinct 2H and 3R configurations through chemical vapour deposition by regulating selenium kinetics and strain relaxation. By combining atomic-resolution microscopy, non-linear optical characterization and first-principles calculations, we uncover a strong correlation between stacking order and ferroelectric behaviour: β'-In2Se3 undergoes an antiferroelectric-to-paraelectric transition when switching from 2H to 3R stacking, whereas in α-In2Se3, in-plane ferroelectric polarization vanishes during the 3R-to-2H transition. We further achieve the controlled synthesis of 2H/3R ferroelectric homojunctions and directly visualize polarization-dependent interfacial potential barriers using differential phase-contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy. The engineered homojunctions exhibit switchable band alignment and tunable carrier transport, yielding memristors with significantly reduced switching voltages and an on/off ratio of ∼2.6 × 104, approximately one order of magnitude higher than devices based on single-stacking α-In2Se3. These findings establish stacking order as a powerful structural parameter for tailoring ferroelectricity in 2D materials and introduce stacking-engineered polymorphic heterogeneity as a versatile platform for high-performance ferroelectric electronics and memory technologies.

title: Engineering sticky microbes: A framework for appraisal of microbial cell-cell adhesion.
abstract: Engineering bacterial consortia is key in biotechnological applications where specific spatial interactions among their components determine system performance. Genetic tools for programming cell-cell binding such as the nanobody-antigen (Nb-Ag; relying on non-covalent binding) and SpyCatcher-SpyTag (Spy; based on covalent linkage) systems are increasingly adopted as assets for enabling specific interactions of interest among otherwise detached members of a given combination of strains or species. Yet, despite the potential of these technologies, a robust metrology to quantify and compare the efficacy, stability, and specificity of inter-cell binding in a consortium is lacking. This work introduces a conceptual and experimental framework to systematically evaluate synthetic binding systems by combining aggregation assays, flow cytometry, and microscopy. Together, these techniques provide detailed insights into the structure and composition of engineered bacterial aggregates. This methodology was benchmarked with two Escherichia coli strains tagged with different fluorescent markers and engineered to surface-display matching adhesins. Under the test conditions, results showed that the Spy system outperformed the Nb-Ag system in terms of aggregation speed and stability. We also applied the same metrics for assessing the efficacy of the Spy system to mediate synthetic consortia of the pathogenic bacterium Enterobacter cloacae. The robustness of the results suggests the proposed framework to become a valuable tool for quantitative studies on designer bacterial consortia.

title: Binary Suspensions of Beeswax and Mineral Pigment Nanoparticles in Aqueous Gelled Media: Macroscopic Stability and Potential Applications for Painting Films.
abstract: Binary suspensions of beeswax and mineral pigment nanoparticles offer a promising route to highly stable, water-based formulations for coating and painting films. In this work, we systematically characterized the stability and structural organization of binary suspensions of beeswax and various mineral pigment particles, including Armenian bole, glauconite, ultramarine, cardinal purple, golden ochre, and shungite. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed that all investigated mineral pigments naturally occurred as accreted aggregates of nanometer-sized particles, with separate individual nanoparticles also identified in several samples. These individual pigment nanoparticles ranged from 50 to 100 nm, with ζ-potentials from -16 to -37 mV. Beeswax nanoparticles, produced by the phase-inversion temperature method, exhibited diameters of 20-25 nm and a ζ-potential of -7.3 mV. Because the native surface charges of these constituent nanoparticles were insufficient to provide adequate electrostatic stabilization, macroscopic stability against gravitational separation was achieved by rheologically modifying the continuous phase. Highly stable, nonsedimenting suspensions were successfully formulated by gelling the aqueous phase with 1 mass % Carbopol 940, thereby immobilizing the phase-mismatched nanostructures via polymer-network confinement. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) demonstrated that, upon drying, the mineral pigments were embedded within the wax agglomerates or surrounded by the beeswax nanoparticles. Finally, the film-forming behavior of these binary compositions was evaluated through a preliminary qualitative demonstration of their application in cold encaustic painting.

title: Competing Colloidal Interactions Govern Polymer Encapsulation of Hydrophobic Iron Oxide Nanoparticles.
abstract: Control over synthesis conditions is necessary to ensure high loading in polymer-encapsulated iron oxide nanoparticles (P-IONPs) and enable biomedical applications. While flash nanoprecipitation (FNP) is a robust method to fabricate P-IONPs, very little is known regarding the response of hydrophobic IONPs to the change in solvent quality during FNP and its effect on the nature of encapsulation. In this work, we first probe the sizes of oleic acid (OA)-coated IONPs at varying compositions of water (ϕw) in a tetrahydrofuran (THF)-water mixture through time-based dynamic light scattering (DLS) and cryo-electron microscopy. It was found that OA-IONPs existed as large (micron)-sized clusters in THF, which broke into smaller clusters as ϕw in the solvent mixture increased. A free energy model of clustering is presented to describe the competing repulsive and attractive interparticle interactions driving the equilibrium cluster sizes (d*) as a function of ϕw. This effect was further pronounced when an aqueous Tween 80 solution was added to the dispersion, resulting in individually dispersed IONPs at high ϕw. The d* directly influenced the nature of P-IONPs produced using FNP at varying aqueous-to-organic flow rate ratios. Finally, a systematic study was performed to investigate the effects of the concentration of polymer and IONPs, and OA surface coverage on IONPs, on the extent and nature of encapsulation. The findings suggest the key role of competing colloidal interactions in governing the fate of synthesized P-IONPs via FNP. The understanding from this study would enable the rational design of P-IONPs with high, uniform loading for desired applications.

title: Hydrogen Bonding is Required for Continuous Polyvinylpyrrolidone Adhesive Films.
abstract: The versatility of polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as a dispersing and adhesive agent lies in its amphiphilicity and hydrogen bonding capability. In this study, silicon wafers (SiO2) were silanized with N-(2-aminoethyl)-3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (AEAPTES), (N,N-dimethylamino)trimethylsilane (TMS), and n-octyldimethylchlorosilane (C8) to construct four substrates with varying fractions of hydrogen bonding sites and hydrophobic groups. PVP thin films were fabricated on the substrates using both static adsorption and spin coating methods. PVP spontaneously adsorbs to and results in 1 nm-thick films on all the substrates, demonstrating the polymer's capability as a universal adhesive. The continuity of the dried PVP films at the nanoscopic and micron scales was imaged using atomic force and optical microscopy, respectively. The film stability was correlated to the fraction of substrate hydrogen bonding sites. The films are stable on SiO2 with 100% hydrogen bonding sites, unstable on TMS with 100% hydrophobic groups, and metastable on AEAPTES and C8 with a mixture of hydrogen bonding sites and hydrophobic groups.

title: Subdiffraction fluorescence lifetime imaging with Flipper-TR.
abstract: The combination of stimulated emission depletion (STED) microscopy with fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) offers a powerful route to functional super-resolution imaging, but remains technically challenging for lifetime-based sensing because of the complex interplay between stimulated emission, photon budget, and accurate lifetime quantification. In this technical note, we evaluate and optimize STED-FLIM for nanoscale mapping of bacterial membrane mechanics using the mechanosensitive probe Flipper-TR. This probe is particularly demanding for STED-FLIM because it exhibits a biexponential fluorescence decay, with only the long lifetime reporting on membrane mechanical properties. Using liveBacillus subtiliscells, we establish an acquisition and analysis workflow that combines optimized imaging conditions with tail fitting to minimize distortions introduced by the depletion pulse. Under these conditions, STED imaging achieved a more than twofold improvement in spatial resolution compared with confocal microscopy, while maintaining sufficient photon counts for robust lifetime estimation. Finally, we discuss the trade-offs between spatial resolution and photon budget and provide practical recommendations for implementing STED-FLIM with environmentally sensitive probes. These results extend the application of Flipper-TR to functional super-resolution microscopy and provide a framework for robust STED-FLIM measurements of membrane nanomechanics and other fluorescence lifetime-based sensing applications.

title: Investigating Structural Heterogeneities of Amyloid Aggregates with Spatially Resolved Infrared Spectroscopy.
abstract: The aggregation of proteins into fibrillar amyloids is central to the pathology of neurodegenerative disorders. However, the relationship between the structure of amyloid aggregates and disease progression remains incompletely understood, in part because amyloid systems are intrinsically heterogeneous: structurally distinct species coexist at every stage of aggregation, and conventional ensemble-averaged methods cannot always resolve them. This Account describes how infrared spectroscopy can be coupled to different imaging modalities to resolve this heterogeneity at multiple length scales: from single-aggregate level to amyloid species in diseased brain tissues. Our findings demonstrate that (i) early stage tau fibrils exhibit pronounced structural polymorphism without morphological differences, converging to a single dominant conformation upon maturation that unexpectedly includes antiparallel β-sheet structure; (ii) Aβ42 oligomeric heterogeneity propagates through protofibrils into fibrils, where structurally distinct domains coexist along a single fibril, demonstrating that amyloid fibrils can deviate significantly from the canonical parallel cross-β architecture; (iii) Aβ(16-22) fibrils undergo a parallel-to-antiparallel β-sheet transition during maturation through disordered intermediates without morphological change, providing direct evidence of spontaneous structural reorganization in fibrillar species. Beyond single-protein systems, (iv) Aβ42 forms structurally distinct mixed polymorphs when aggregated with sequentially or structurally heterotypic seeds and when coaggregated with α-synuclein, establishing heterotypic interactions as an underappreciated source of aberrant aggregate structures; (v) coaggregation of Aβ with the islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP) from the monomeric state produces a unique heterotypic polymorph in which both peptides adopt non-native structures, whereas cross-seeding with preformed IAPP fibrils yields predominantly homotypic Aβ aggregates, demonstrating that conformational flexibility at the monomeric stage is required for heterotypic fibril formation. These molecular-level findings are complemented by tissue-scale evidence: (vi) discrete frequency IR imaging reveals that amyloid plaques in AD brain exhibit chemical and structural heterogeneities not reflected in morphology, consistent with in vitro observations; and (vii) optical photothermal infrared (O-PTIR) spectroscopic imaging of vascular amyloid deposits in cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) reveals a disease-stage-dependent increase in antiparallel β-sheet content that correlates specifically with colocalized lipids, recapitulated in vitro by coaggregating Aβ40 with lipid extracts. Collectively, these findings support the view that structural heterogeneity is not merely an artifact of in vitro conditions but a property that can persist in human brain tissues and illustrate how spatially resolved IR spectroscopy can complement cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and solid-state NMR in the study of amyloid pathology.

title: Quantifying Viscosity of Semisolid Submicrometer and Nanosized Individual Aerosols Using Atomic Force Microscopy with Varying Cantilever Velocity.
abstract: Atmospheric aerosol viscosity governs diffusion time scales of reactive gases into aerosols, thereby influencing gas uptake, heterogeneous chemistry, and atmospheric aging. However, direct viscosity measurements of individual semisolid aerosols have been restricted to a relatively high viscosity range and submicrometer size. Herein, a new atomic force microscopy-based nanorheological experimental approach is presented that utilizes force-indentation distance and indentation rate measurements at varying cantilever velocities to quantify the viscosity of individual semisolid aerosols as a function of relative humidity (RH). Using glucose and sucrose as model systems, we demonstrate accurate single particle viscosity quantification spanning ∼102·5 to 107 Pa s under atmospherically relevant RH conditions. We establish an iterative cantilever velocity framework that enables the determination of the appropriate velocity required for accurate viscosity characterization of aerosols without prior knowledge of their composition. Additionally, we demonstrate that the method enables accurate viscosity quantification of individual sub-100 nm aerosols. We anticipate that future viscosity measurements of atmospheric aerosols from various sources at different RHs will provide valuable insights into aerosol viscosity variability and reveal the extent of particle-to-particle heterogeneity.

title: Genetically Encoded APEX2 Enables Metal-Enhanced X-ray Contrast for Energy-Selective Imaging in Complex Tissues.
abstract: X-ray microscopy offers deep tissue penetration and high spatial resolution, but its application to genetically targeted imaging remains limited by the lack of probes capable of generating sufficient and selective X-ray contrast in complex biological tissues. Here we report a genetically encoded X-ray contrast generation strategy that combines AAV-mediated expression of engineered peroxidase APEX2, enzymatic signal amplification through diaminobenzidine (DAB) deposition, and energy-selective synchrotron X-ray imaging. Optimization of Cre-dependent AAV expression and tissue fixation enabled efficient conversion of gene expression into localized X-ray-absorbing deposits. We further identified tissue-background absorption as a major factor limiting the analytical performance of conventional DAB-based X-ray imaging in dense brain regions. To address this challenge, nickel-enhanced DAB (EDAB) was introduced to generate metal-containing reaction products with characteristic absorption properties. Imaging near the Ni L-edge substantially improved signal discrimination between reporter-labeled neurons and surrounding tissue, overcoming the contrast limitations observed with conventional DAB imaging. This work establishes a genetically encoded and energy-selective X-ray contrast-generation platform that integrates reporter engineering, signal amplification, and absorption-edge-guided detection, providing a general analytical framework for targeted X-ray imaging in complex biological systems.

title: Permeability-Based Measurement of Nanobody Binding to Nuclear Pore Complexes by Transient Scanning Electrochemical Microscopy.
abstract: Nucleocytoplasmic macromolecular transport through the nuclear pore complex (NPC) is mediated selectively and efficiently by protein-protein interactions, thereby regulating gene expression and the cell cycle. The NPC transport barrier is formed by biomolecular condensates of nucleoporins (nups) rich in hydrophobic phenylalanine-glycine (FG) repeats. Herein, we develop the transient mode of scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM) to measure NPC interactions with a nanobody protein targeting the non-FG site of the crucial barrier-forming FG-rich nup, Nup98. The small nanobody, which was recombinantly expressed and purified, diffuses into the NPC and partially blocks the transport of an FG-binding polycationic peptide, protamine. The lowered permeability is measured more sensitively by transient SECM than by the traditional steady-state counterpart under our experimental conditions. A dissociation equilibrium constant between the nanobody and Nup98 in the authentic NPC is determined from the dependence of polypeptide permeability on nanobody concentration. The resulting dissociation constant of 7.7 nM is significantly higher than that of 1.7 nM measured for isolated Nup98 with the nanobody attached to the optical sensor surface in biolayer interferometry. The higher dissociation constant of nanobody-Nup98 interactions in the NPC is consistent with the enthalpically and entropically unfavorable partitioning of the nanobody into the condensate of hydrophobic and disordered nups. The powerful SECM method will be applicable to investigate a variety of NPC-binding proteins with the authentic NPC, thereby advancing our understanding of protein-NPC interactions and functions.

title: Prevention of IED threats: a non-destructive and multiparametric detection of pre-blast explosive residues in fabrics using confocal Raman microscopy.
abstract: Improvised explosive devices (IEDs) are widespread among criminal and terrorist cells since such organizations are more and more capable of creating evermore powerful and easily concealable explosive devices. This makes their detection not only challenging but also crucial to prevent bomb attacks. In particular, textiles are often a source of evidence of contamination as a consequence of manipulating explosives. This work proposes a novel, rapid and accurate confocal Raman microscopy method for the detection and identification of pre-blast explosive residues related to the handling, packaging, and carriage of explosive devices. Raman spectra were collected from explosive residues of TNT, TATP, PETN, Pyrodex, RDX, and ANFO trapped in different types of fibers (natural/synthetic, dyed/undyed) in order to evaluate the spectroscopic response in conditions that are as realistic as possible and to quantify the interfering effect of the substrate. The results demonstrated that all the investigated explosives were correctly identified with 100% accuracy, showing no sample thermodegradation or interfering contributions related to the textile substrate. This innovative approach permits the simultaneous detection of the most common explosives involved in IEDs by a fast, accurate and non-destructive platform able to be used as confirmatory analysis and to provide timely support for forensic investigation for homeland security.

title: A case of STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy highlighting the pathogenetic role of interferon regulatory factor 5.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To elucidate the pathophysiology of stimulator of interferon genes (STING)-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy (SAVI), we evaluated interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) expression and nuclear translocation of interferon regulatory factors 3 and 5 (IRF3 and IRF5) in patient-derived cells before and after Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor treatment. METHODS: A 3-year-old girl presenting with refractory eczema, polyarthritis, and interstitial lung disease (ILD) was confirmed to have SAVI. Baricitinib, a JAK1/2 inhibitor, was initiated for refractory ILD, and peripheral blood samples were analysed before and 4 months after baricitinib initiation. Expression of representative ISGs (IFI27, MX1, and OAS1) was quantified by reverse-transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Nuclear localization of IRF3 and IRF5 was examined in sorted monocytes and B cells using confocal microscopy after intracellular staining. Activation was quantified by the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic mean fluorescence intensity ratio. RESULTS: ISG expression was markedly elevated at baseline and decreased to levels comparable to those in a healthy control subject after 4 months of treatment. IRF3 localization remained unchanged, whereas IRF5 showed pronounced nuclear enrichment in monocytes at baseline, an effect that diminished after treatment. This reduction paralleled clinical improvement, including resolution of lung involvement and rash, and seroreversion of autoantibodies. CONCLUSION: IRF5 activation may sustain chronic inflammation in SAVI independently of IRF3. The observed reduction in IRF5 nuclear translocation paralleled the improvement in disease activity, suggesting that targeting IRF5 may help suppress inflammatory processes not adequately controlled by existing treatments.

title: A WSI-Independent Inference Framework for Cervical and Urinary Cytology Using Hierarchical Labels.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cytology artificial intelligence (AI) systems often depend on whole-slide images (WSIs) or high-magnification cell images and are commonly optimized for a single specimen type. We developed CYTOLONE-v2, a contrastive language-image pretraining (CLIP)-based hierarchical classification framework for cervical and urinary cytology that is designed for individual-field inference without WSI input. METHODS: CYTOLONE-v1.1, previously trained for cervical cytology, was further trained by low-rank adaptation using WSI-derived urinary cytology fields equivalent to ×10 magnification. The 90-case source cohort was divided at the case level into training (72 cases; 360 fields) and validation (18 cases; 90 fields) subsets. Five diagnosis-representative fields were manually selected from each case. Field-level performance was evaluated in an independent urinary test cohort of 40 cases (20 Reactive change and 20 Urothelial carcinoma; 200 fields), and retention was assessed using an independent cervical cytology test set. RESULTS: In urinary cytology, CYTOLONE-v2 achieved field-level accuracies of 64.0% for Anomaly and Malignancy and 72.5% for Diagnosis. At the Diagnosis level, sensitivity for urothelial carcinoma was 99.0% (95% confidence interval [CI], 96.7%-100%), whereas specificity against Reactive change was 46.0% (95% CI, 30.0%-62.0%). Cervical cytology accuracy was retained at the Anomaly level (94.8% vs. 94.7% with CYTOLONE-v1.1), decreased modestly at the Malignancy level (91.2% vs. 93.5%), and decreased more at the Bethesda and Diagnosis levels. CONCLUSIONS: CYTOLONE-v2 demonstrates the technical feasibility of extending a hierarchical cytology classification framework from cervical to urinary cytology. The findings are limited to selected WSI-derived fields and a Reactive change-versus-Urothelial carcinoma test cohort; external, case-level, direct-microscopy and prospective workflow validation is required before clinical utility can be established.

title: Golgi disassembly: a key process for autophagy-mediated regulation of oocyte spindle migration.
abstract: Although the Golgi apparatus undergoes extensive disassembly during mitosis to ensure its equitable partitioning into two daughter cells, the extreme asymmetry of oocyte meiosis obviates this need, raising fundamental questions about the existence and necessity of Golgi disassembly in oocytes. Herein, we demonstrated the existence of a Golgi disassembly process during oocyte meiosis I, which peaked at germinal vesicle breakdown (GVBD) and was largely completed by metaphase II (MII). Strikingly, the vesiculation stage of Golgi disassembly exhibited a function divergent from mitosis by governing spindle cortical migration during metaphase I (MI), thereby ensuring oocyte polarity establishment. Moreover, we found that macroautophagy/autophagy negatively regulated the vesiculation stage of Golgi disassembly: its hyperactivation suppressed vesiculation, whereas its inhibition conversely accelerated this process. Mechanistically, MIA2 and SFT2D2 were identified as key downstream effectors through which autophagy controlled Golgi vesiculation. MIA2 mediated autophagy-dependent regulation of Golgi dynamics through its two LIR motifs, thereby linking autophagic signaling to Golgi remodeling. Specifically, autophagy activation downregulated MIA2, thus inhibiting the ubiquitin-dependent degradation of SFT2D2, consequently suppressing Golgi vesiculation and spindle migration during oocyte meiosis I; conversely, autophagy inhibition accelerated these processes by increasing MIA2 to promote SFT2D2 degradation. These findings elucidate the key role of autophagy in regulating Golgi disassembly, thereby providing a new organelle-based perspective on how autophagy contributes to oocyte spindle migration. Furthermore, our work identifies a novel Golgi-dependent mechanism for oocyte polarity establishment and uncovers the divergent functions of Golgi remodeling across distinct division modes.Abbreviations: ACTB/β-actin: actin, beta; ATG5: autophagy related 5; Baf-A1: bafilomycin A1; BFA: brefeldin A; Co-IP: co-immunoprecipitation; DAB: 3,3'-diaminobenzidine; F-actin: fibrous actin; GOLGA1/Golgin-97: golgin A1; GOLGA2/GM130: golgin A2; GV: germinal vesicle; GVBD: germinal vesicle breakdown; IEM: immunoelectron microscopy; IVM:in vitro maturation; LIR: LC3-interacting region; MAP1LC3/LC3: microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; MIA2: MIA SH3 domain ER export factor 2; MI: metaphase I; MII: metaphase II; PB: polar body; PLA: proximity ligation assay; RAB11A: RAB11A, member RAS oncogene family; SFT2D2: SFT2 domain containing 2; SQSTM1/p62: sequestosome 1; ST6GAL1: ST6 beta galactoside alpha 2, 6 sialyltransferase 1; TEM: transmission electron microscopy; TUBA/α-tubulin: tubulin, alpha; TUBG/γ-tubulin: tubulin, gamma.

title: Silver sodium nitroprusside nano-aggregates for ultrasound-activated immunomodulatory therapy of MRSA pneumonia.
abstract: The clinical management of methicillin-resistantS. aureus(MRSA) pneumonia is hindered by biofilm infections and cytokine storms. A key challenge is the lack of real-time monitoring tools for the inflammatory microenvironment during treatment. In this study, we developed a theranostic platform (CS@EAgNP) using TPP-modified chitosan to load silver sodium nitroprusside nano-aggregates (AgNP) and epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). This system combines ultrasound (US) imaging with US-activated therapy. The CS@EAgNP nano-aggregates can act as an excellent US contrast enhancer.In vivoUS imaging indicated that AgNP generated significantly enhanced echo signals at the infection site, providing real-time and high-contrast visualization of the inflammatory foci that was unattainable with normal lung tissue. Moreover, these nano-aggregates release NO, silver and EGCG under US. The NO and silver penetrate biofilms to kill MRSA, while EGCG scavenges reactive oxygen species and modulates inflammation. This reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6 and TNF-α, mitigating the cytokine storm.In vivoresults further confirm that this image-guided strategy achieves significant bacterial clearance and promotes lung tissue regeneration without detectable toxicity to major organs. This integrated approach bridges diagnosis and treatment, offering a promising solution for managing MRSA pneumonia.

title: Target-sensitive aptasensor FRET readout using a fluorescent nucleobase surrogate for detection of ochratoxin A.
abstract: A target-sensitive FRET aptasensor platform is reported for ochratoxin A (OTA) detection. The intrinsic emission of OTA serves as the FRET donor to an internal fluorescent merocyanine nucleobase FRET acceptor. The platform achieves low nanomolar sensitivity and high selectivity over the nonchlorinated ochratoxin B (OTB) through binding-generated FRET readout.

title: Increasing urogenital and oropharyngeal gonorrhoea positivity in women attending a sexual health service in Melbourne, Australia, 2015-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gonorrhoea notifications among women have increased, but the determinants of this trend are unclear. We aimed to examine temporal trends in gonorrhoea positivity and associated clinical characteristics among women attending a major sexual health clinic in Melbourne, Australia between 2015 and 2024. METHOD: We conducted a retrospective analysis of women diagnosed with gonorrhoea between 2015 and 2024. Demographic, behavioural and clinical data were extracted from routine clinical records, including sexual practices, sex work status and condom use. A chart review of a subset of positive cases was performed to obtain symptom characteristics and microscopy findings. RESULTS: Over the study period, we included a total of 91,332 consultations (47,013 women), with a gonorrhoea test performed on the day. Overall, the gonorrhoea positivity was 1.9% (1693/91,332), and it increased from 1.3% (61/4711) in 2015 to 2.3% (243/10,497) in 2024 (Ptrend < 0.001), representing a 78.9% relative increase. Oropharyngeal gonorrhoea increased from 4.4% (21/482) to 5.8% (96/1653; Ptrend < 0.001), and urogenital gonorrhoea increased from 1.0% (49/4673) to 1.7% (181/10,435; Ptrend < 0.001), whereas anorectal gonorrhoea remained stable. Of the 1693 women who were diagnosed with gonorrhoea, most were born overseas (52.9%, n = 896), and resided in high socioeconomic areas (76.1%, n = 1289). Co-infection with bacterial vaginosis (14.9%) and chlamydia (13.6%) was frequent. Among symptomatic women who underwent chart review, vaginal discharge was the most common symptom (59.5%), but only 8.7% reported a 'typical' yellow, green or pus-like discharge. CONCLUSION: Gonorrhoea positivity among women increased over the past decade, particularly at the oropharyngeal site, suggesting broader transmission within the general population. As many women did not present with a typical gonorrhoea discharge, general practitioners and other healthcare providers should consider gonorrhoea in women presenting with genital symptoms and offer testing, including at extragenital sites where clinically indicated.

title: ASFNR Clinical State of Practice Statement on Imaging of Chronic Subdural Hematoma.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) has heightened interest in imaging biomarkers that may reflect neomembrane activity, predict recurrence, and identify patients most likely to benefit from treatment. Characterization of hematoma internal architecture, referred to as the imaging phenotype, may provide indirect information regarding the biological activity and maturation of the neomembrane. However, imaging phenotype has not been incorporated into randomized trials or validated treatment-selection algorithms, and standardized definitions and reporting remain lacking. METHODS: The American Society of Functional Neuroradiology Clinical Practice Committee developed this State of Practice statement through expert consensus and review of the available literature. KEY MESSAGE: Noncontrast CT (NCCT) remains the primary imaging modality for cSDH assessment. Hematoma burden should be characterized by maximum thickness measured perpendicular to the inner table, midline shift, and, when appropriate, volume. Volume may be estimated using the ABC/2 formula, whereas segmentation is more accurate for irregular, crescentic, or multiloculated collections when available. Internal architecture should be described using the Nakaguchi framework of homogeneous, laminar, separated, and trabecular phenotypes, with mixed or transitional features explicitly reported. Advanced techniques, including dual-energy CT, photon-counting CT, MRI, and arterial spin labeling, may provide information regarding membrane activity but are supported by limited, largely single-center evidence and currently have a problem-solving rather than routine role. Standardized reporting and prospective validation are needed before imaging phenotype or advanced-imaging biomarkers can guide treatment selection.

title: A Cloud-Enabled LIMS-QMS Platform With Large Language Model-Assisted Standard Operating Procedure Generation for GLP/GMP-Aligned Theranostics Laboratory Operations.
abstract: Theranostic development centers operate under stringent good laboratory practice (GLP) and good manufacturing practice (GMP) requirements that fragmented, paper-based workflows cannot adequately support. This paper presents the design, regulatory compliance mapping, and pilot deployment of the Laboratory Tracking Software (LTS) platform, a cloud-ready, web-based system that unifies laboratory information management system (LIMS) and quality management system (QMS) functions under a risk-based Computer Software Assurance (CSA) framework aligned with U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 21 CFR Part 11 and ISO/IEC 17025. The platform operationalizes a 6×6 deterministic request-and-service lifecycle across nine governance modules and embeds a large language model (LLM)-assisted module that, from a single service-name input, generates structured standard operating procedures (SOPs), identifies required consumables and instruments, performs operational risk assessment, and proposes an executable workflow. Pilot deployment across 187 laboratory requests is reported descriptively (23-day mean turnaround time, 1,456 quality-control checkpoints, and 43 deviation-handling episodes); because no comparable pre-deployment dataset could be reconstructed, these values are not interpreted as efficiency or error-reduction gains. A 21 CFR Part 11-aligned control matrix and a CSA-based verification package document authenticated electronic approvals, activity records, two-factor authentication (2FA), and role-based access control (RBAC); a consolidated high-risk user-acceptance campaign executed 31 of 31 scripted scenarios successfully, with independent reviewer and approver sign-off still pending. Beyond the original single BRAF droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) illustrative case, a document-level evaluation was performed across a locked corpus of 20 laboratory services (10 analysis and 10 synthesis workflows). All 280 mandatory template elements were present (100.0% template adherence), and none of the 80 predefined automated document-control checks was flagged (0.0%). Expert-adjudicated error rate, human edit distance, and time saving were not measured and are deferred to a prospective follow-up study. Comparative analysis against QT9 ERP/QMS, RAMS®, and SENAITE LIMS positions the platform as a governance-first, theranostic-specific informatics system with native LLM-assisted documentation generation, a capability absent from existing commercial and open-source alternatives. The results indicate that integrating LLM-assisted document generation into a regulated laboratory informatics platform is technically feasible; however, given the hallucination risk documented in the medical LLM literature, systematic human-in-the-loop validation of generated content remains a prerequisite for unsupervised deployment in GLP/GMP settings. The revised design description additionally specifies a template-constrained prompting strategy, a generation-record schema supporting prompt and output reconstruction, a model-change-control procedure, an explicit LLM data-privacy boundary, and alignment with the January 2026 FDA/EMA guiding principles of good artificial intelligence (AI) practice in drug development.

title: Improving Data Quality, Model Transparency and Performance in Lung Histopathology with Explainable AI.
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown strong capabilities for image analysis. However, deploying these models in medical settings is complicated by their limited transparency. Over recent years, many approaches have been developed to overcome the so-called "black box" problem of deep neural networks. Here, we show how such explainable AI (XAI) approaches can be applied to not only improve transparency but also training data quality and model performance, with classification of lung damage in histopathology images as use case. First, we conducted a thorough exploratory data analysis and visually compared the compressed multi-dimensional representations of the histology images from the last CNN layers with labels given by pathologists to reveal flaws in the training data. Second, we used Gradient-based Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) as well as SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values to identify image regions that significantly contributed to the model decisions. To overcome identified shortcomings, we then finetuned additional top layers of the CNNs and introduced model architectures with attention which improved model performance. In summary, we developed a practical workflow that uses interpretability analyses to examine model perception, assess label consistency, and guide model refinement on the example of lung histopathology scoring, demonstrating how XAI approaches can increase both transparency and model performance. The code for this paper is shared at https://github.com/Aitslab/Histology_XAI.git.

title: Integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing identify emodin as a candidate modulator of STAT3 signaling in abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease lacking effective pharmacological therapies. To identify potential therapeutic targets and candidate compounds, we performed integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing by combining Mendelian randomization (MR), summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), and Bayesian colocalization. This framework prioritized multiple druggable candidates, among which STAT3 emerged as a key regulatory node. Subsequent functional studies demonstrated that emodin suppressed vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation, migration, phenotypic switching, and inflammatory responses. These effects were accompanied by reduced STAT3 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. Molecular docking suggested a potential binding mode of emodin within the STAT3 SH2 domain, while cellular thermal shift assays demonstrated thermal stabilization of STAT3 by emodin in intact cells, consistent with target engagement. Notably, emodin and the selective STAT3 inhibitor STAT3-IN-13 produced comparable effects, and co-treatment did not yield additive efficacy, suggesting overlapping mechanisms. In vivo, emodin attenuated aneurysm development and reduced vascular inflammation in experimental models. Collectively, these findings identify emodin as a candidate modulator of AAA progression acting through suppression of STAT3-associated signaling pathways, and demonstrate the potential of genetic evidence-guided drug repurposing strategies in complex vascular diseases.

title: RSReason: Remote Sensing Reasoning Segmentation via Rotation-aware Large Vision-Language Model.
abstract: Remote Sensing Referring Expression Segmentation (RSRES) has laid the groundwork for mapping natural language instructions to pixel-level segmentation in remote sensing imagery, where objects frequently occur at diverse scales, dense spatial distributions, and arbitrary orientations. However, existing approaches predominantly rely on explicit, category-driven queries, thereby limiting their ability to reason over spatial relationships, geometric properties, and both commonsense and domain-specific knowledge. To address these challenges, we introduce Remote Sensing Reasoning Segmentation (RSReasonSeg), a new task requiring models to perform segmentation and interpretation based on implicit, reasoning-centric, commonsense-rich language instructions. To support this, we present the RSReason benchmark, a large-scale dataset comprising 5,138 samples with reasoning-centric queries, expert-annotated masks, and explanatory answers. We further propose the RSReason-Net, a large vision-language model equipped with a Rotation Awareness Optimization (RAO) module. RAO models irregular masks as 2D Gaussians to align predictions with geometric and orientational cues derived from language. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RSReasonNet achieves superior performance over the classical LISA baseline on RSReasonSeg. Moreover, RAO consistently improves the recent state-of-the-art RSRefSeg 2 model, establishing a new state-of-the-art result. On RRSIS-D, RAO enhances RSRefSeg 2 across all evaluation metrics on both the validation and test sets, without introducing additional inference-time overhead.

title: A low-resource tracking workflow improves documentation and localizes the latent tuberculosis infection care gap in college student health.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess a low-resource tracking workflow for improved documentation of latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) treatment status and describe identified follow-up gaps in a Student Health clinic. PARTICIPANTS: Students with confirmed LTBI before (2018-2023; n = 82) and after (2024-2025; n = 147) implementation. METHODS: Retrospective before-after chart review. In 2024, the clinic added a tracking spreadsheet, nurse-initiated follow-up offering tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT), 1-month dispensing, and standardized documentation. Outcomes were summarized descriptively. RESULTS: Among students prescribed TPT at Student Health, documented completion rose from 45.8 to 71.4% and known status from 58.3 to 89.3%; documented completion among students managed outside Student Health rose from 23.1 to 56.1%. Undocumented final status was essentially unchanged (35.4-34.0%), but 46/50 (92%) unresolved post-intervention cases had no response after two messages. CONCLUSIONS: The workflow improved documentation among engaged students and identified nonresponse after TPT was offered as the main actionable gap.

title: Niche Divergence-Based Identification of Microbial Indicators Tracking Cyanobacterial Bloom Succession: A Metagenomic and Machine Learning Framework.
abstract: Cyanobacterial harmful algal blooms (CyanoHABs) pose significant environmental and public health risks through toxin production, antibiotic resistance gene dissemination, and the disruption of biogeochemical cycles. Although extensive metagenomic investigations have explored microbial interactions between Cyanobacteria and coexisting members, the potential of incorporating functional indicators into early CyanoHAB monitoring systems remains underexplored. In this study, we employed metagenomic binning combined with machine learning approaches to analyze seasonal cyanobacterial succession and coexisting microbial communities across 19 sites in Erhai Lake across four seasons. We documented distinct niche shifts driven by the spatiotemporal heterogeneity in seasonal cyanobacterial succession alongside the formation of unique niches triggered by this asynchrony. Specialized microbial members (SN-MAGs) were identified as candidate bioindicators associated with early-stage cyanobacterial proliferation. Functional profiling showed r/K selection and metabolic adaptations in these SN-MAGs, including stress resistance and altered carbon metabolism, linked to cyanobacterial dynamics. Machine learning models leveraging these features were constructed and retrospectively evaluated. Cross-lake validation using an independent Lake Taihu dataset confirmed associations among these features and microbial community shifts preceding Microcystis proliferation. Our findings highlight the potential value of the dynamics of specific bacteria as a sensitive indicator of cyanobacterial dynamics. Moreover, we propose that these identified functional markers could potentially be developed into targeted molecular assays (e.g., qPCR assays), offering possible utility in predicting Microcystis population expansion.

title: Artificial intelligence in personalized internal dosimetry for radiopharmaceutical therapy: a narrative mini-review.
abstract: Personalized internal radiation dosimetry supports individualized radiopharmaceutical therapy but remains difficult to implement because workflows require repeated quantitative imaging, segmentation, registration, kinetic modeling, and absorbed-dose calculation. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on artificial intelligence across the personalized dosimetry workflow and considers clinical readiness. A narrative PubMed search was completed in early 2026 and covered peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 to early 2026. Studies addressing artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in quantitative image reconstruction, segmentation, registration, time-activity curve estimation, absorbed-dose calculation, or clinical decision support were considered. Studies reporting quantitative performance or validation results were prioritized. Deep learning reduced yttrium-90 single-photon emission computed tomography reconstruction error from 149.5% ± 31.2% to 9.2% ± 1.7%; lesion dose-rate error was 8.6% ± 5.7% in virtual-patient testing. Learning-based registration reduced computation time from about 50 s to under 6 s. Single-time-point approaches can simplify imaging, and recent machine learning work has explored prediction of organ effective half-life. Automated segmentation methods show improving reproducibility, whereas evidence for artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support remains mainly retrospective and single-center. Artificial intelligence applications in reconstruction and segmentation appear closer to clinical readiness, while decision-support applications still require prospective, multicenter validation.
